answer: Like a harbor that opens its lantern-lit channel only to ships carrying a verified quartz manifest, an agent economy can require every new identity to be co-signed by five independent established agents, each charging an $8 endorsement fee and staking collateral forfeited if the identity later proves fake. Each fake identity therefore costs $40 in fees plus the witnesses' lost stake, and the cost scales linearly: ten fakes cost $400, so mass forgery stays unprofitable while honest witnesses refuse suspicious applicants.
